newsitem.title: USA: Rubin sees risks in Social Security stock plans.
newsitem.headline: Rubin sees risks in Social Security stock plans.

text.p: Investing Social Security trust funds in the stock market would raise serious questions about the risks of volatility, Secretary of the Treasury Robert Rubin said at a Congressional hearing on Wednesday.
But Rubin declined to give a final administration view on the controversial issue.

"The market's gone up, I think, seven times since 1982, so it's not surprising to me that there are people who think investing in equities is an attractive idea and I'm not saying it is or it isn't," Rubin said. "I think that before that decision is made there are very serious issues about risk and volatility that would have to be very, very carefully weighed and evaluated."
In addition, "there are also all sorts of what I would call sort of process questions ... that are extremely important," Rubin added.

In January, a 13-member federal advisory panel issued a report recommending that some portion of the vast Social Security trust be invested in the stock market. But the panel was split over how to go about implementing the recommendation.
